# TftpdR 0.2.0

Second release: the read-only TFTP (RFC 1350) server now uses the standard TFTP
port by default, can listen on several addresses at once, and ships a more
complete native [Slint](https://slint.dev/) desktop panel.

**中文摘要**：第二个公开版本。默认端口改为标准 TFTP 端口 69；支持一个端口上的
多地址监听；GUI 增加首次启动配置引导、独占式「全部网络」地址选择、最近根目录
清空、空闲时配置/根目录变更自动重启，以及产品图标与新的头部配色。配置格式有
破坏性变更：`bind_address` 已删除，改用 `port` + `bind_addresses`。仍不支持
上传、GUI/daemon IPC 与 Windows 服务注册。

| Windows arm64 (MSVC) | `tftpd-r-0.2.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` |

Every archive contains `tftpd-r` (headless daemon), `tftpd-r-gui` (desktop
panel), `config.example.toml`, `README.md`, `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`.
Windows archives also include `tftpd-r-gui.ico` for shortcuts. `SHA256SUMS`
covers all assets in this release.

## What's new

### Default port 69

- The default listen address is now `127.0.0.1:69` (the standard TFTP port),
  replacing 0.1.0's `6969`.
- Binding a privileged port without the required rights fails with a
  non-forcing hint that suggests an unprivileged port (for example `6969`); the
  server never falls back, elevates or rewrites the configuration.
- ADR: [`docs/adr/0007-default-port-69.md`](https://github.com/greyskysoul/tftpd-r/blob/v0.2.0/docs/adr/0007-default-port-69.md).

### Multiple bind addresses

- `port` plus `bind_addresses: Vec<IpAddr>` replaces the single
  `bind_address: SocketAddr`. One port is shared by all listeners (1–16
  addresses); duplicates are removed and `0.0.0.0`/`::` collapse the other
  addresses of their family.
- Binding is all-or-nothing: one unbindable address aborts the whole start
  instead of serving a silently reduced set. Every listener has its own accept
  loop; sessions bound to a specific address reply from that address.
- ADR: [`docs/adr/0008-multiple-bind-addresses.md`](https://github.com/greyskysoul/tftpd-r/blob/v0.2.0/docs/adr/0008-multiple-bind-addresses.md).

### Desktop panel

- First start without a valid `config.toml` opens the settings dialog once per
  user profile; the unconfigured form preselects "全部网络 (0.0.0.0)".
- The bind-address picker treats "全部网络" as exclusive: selecting it clears
  the specific addresses, selecting a specific address clears it, it cannot be
  unchecked, and removing the last specific address selects it again.
- The recent-root drop-down has a 清空 button that clears the local history.
- Saving settings or changing the root restarts a running server automatically
  when no transfer is active. With active transfers the new values are stored
  and the log asks for a manual restart.
- New product icon (`app-icon.svg/png/ico`, Material `dns` glyph) used for the
  window and task-bar icon; the title bar and toolbar share one flat `#37474f`
  block with the `#263238`/`#fafafa` brand mark.
- Fixes: no console window on Windows, status-bar border and progress-fill
  alignment, leaf-directory name in the status bar, upload-disabled notice,
  recent-root drop-down scrolling/elision, and completed transfers always leave
  a log line.
- ADR: [`docs/adr/0009-gui-first-run-and-auto-restart.md`](https://github.com/greyskysoul/tftpd-r/blob/v0.2.0/docs/adr/0009-gui-first-run-and-auto-restart.md).

## Breaking changes

- Configuration files from 0.1.0 use `bind_address = "127.0.0.1:6969"`. That key
  is now rejected as an unknown field; replace it with:

  ```toml
  port = 69
  bind_addresses = ["127.0.0.1"]
  ```

  The daemon `--bind <ADDR>` override replaces the whole list with one address
  and port. Because configuration uses `deny_unknown_fields`, an old file fails
  loudly instead of silently binding the wrong interface.
- The default port changed from 6969 to 69.
- The desktop panel still does not write `config.toml`; values that must survive
  a restart belong in that file.

## Not included (deliberate)

- WRQ uploads: the server answers with ERROR 2 and `allow_upload = true` is a
  configuration error. `netascii`/`mail` are rejected rather than treated as
  `octet`.
- GUI/daemon IPC (the GUI embeds the server in its own process), Windows Service
  registration, system tray, auto-update, remote management and authentication.

## Verification status

Verified by hand on Windows 11 with Rust 1.100.0 `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: **147
tests pass**, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean,
`cargo build --workspace --release` succeeds, and the GUI `--smoke-test` exits
with 0 in debug and release builds.

Manual GUI checks on that machine covered the first-run dialog and its one-time
flag, all bind-address toggle transitions, clearing the recent-root list, a
transfer served from the new root after an idle auto-restart, and the deferred
restart warning while a transfer was active. A web-free raw UDP client (the
in-repo Python client) downloaded files from the running panel; external TFTP
clients were not used.

The `0.2.0` release workflow
([44719989555](https://github.com/greyskysoul/tftpd-r/actions/runs/44719989555))
passed the test gate on Windows MSVC and Linux GNU, built all four archives on
native runners and published them. The SHA-256 digests reported by GitHub for
the four archives match the attached `SHA256SUMS` file. The archives themselves
were not downloaded and executed again in the release session; the MSVC and
arm64 binaries remain unrun.

These artifacts are produced by CI. The `x86_64` archives are built on the same
runners that also run the full test suite (MSVC on Windows, GNU on Linux), so
those two toolchains are known to compile and pass the tests. The `aarch64`
archives are built natively on arm64 runners, but no test suite is executed
there and no arm64 binary was run by hand. In addition, **nothing below has been
verified** and is not claimed by this release:

- running the GUI or daemon on a Linux desktop, or any `aarch64` binary anywhere;
- interoperability with real or legacy external TFTP clients, LAN/`0.0.0.0`
  operation, firewall rules for TID ports, and binding port 69 as an
  unprivileged user;
- RDP sessions, real keyboard/IME input, screen readers, and rendering at other
  DPIs, locales or font stacks.

Linux binaries link the glibc of the CI runner (`ubuntu-latest`); build from
source on older distributions. The GUI needs an X11/Wayland session at runtime;
the daemon does not.

## Checksums

`SHA256SUMS` is attached to this release; verify with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`
or `Get-FileHash` on Windows.
